hexagon : fix DMA transfers with strides > 24 bits ( #31442 ) 
 
 hexagon : fix DMA transfers with strides > 24 bits 
 
 On v75+ the 2D DMA descriptor stores row_size and strides in 24 bits. 
dma_queue_push sent oversized strides to fallback_2d, which only splits 
nrows, so strid
news.aiSummary: The article discusses a bug fix for the Hexagon architecture, addressing an issue where DMA transfers with strides larger than 24 bits caused problems on version 75 and above. The 2D DMA descriptor stores row_size and strides in 24 bits, but dma_queue_push was sending oversized strides to fallback_2d, which only splits nrows, leading to incorrect stride handling. The fix corrects this by ensuring strides fit within the 24-bit limit.

news.title: trunk/57448d9a1e9d4b6c7ba5355242936292727a5cf0: [MPS] Pass ELU params in float (#202904)
news.dek: ELUParams<T> / ELUBackwardParams<T>  passed  alpha ,  scale  and  input_scale  to the kernel as  T , so for half/bfloat16 SELU's constants were rounded before being used in float math, making ~18% (half) / ~83% (bfloat16) of SELU outputs 1 ulp off CPU. Make them plain float struc
news.aiSummary: The patch changes how ELU parameters are passed to the kernel. Previously the parameters were cast to the template type T, causing rounding for half and bfloat16 precision and resulting in many SELU outputs being slightly off from CPU results. The update now passes the parameters as plain float structures, improving accuracy.
